To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a new synthesis method of conducting polymer nanowires, nanotubes, and nanofibres using electrochemical lithography and electrospinning techniques, and studied their size dependent physical properties.
the electronic transport properties of individual nanofibers/nanowires are size dependent and can be controlled by changing the nanowires diameter.

the electronic transport, mechanical, optical, and thermal properties of conducting polymer nanostructures can be significantly modified by changing the nanostructure morphology, size, and surface chemistry.
In summary, our research is concerned with
synthesis and properties of conducting polymer nanowires/tubules and their potential applications.
the synthesis and properties of conducting polymer nanofibers nanorods and nanotubes.
the fabrication, characterization, and potential applications and challenges of conducting polymer nanofibers/nanotubes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the one dimensional nanostructures have great promise for the development of novel devices and applications.

these conducting polymer nanotube and nanofibres have great potential for future applications in the fields of chemical, optical and biosensors, nanoelectronics, energy conversion and storage devices, and biomedical engineering.
the one dimensional nanostructures, especially nanotubes and fibers of conducting polymers, are a very promising and exciting new field with many potential applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the physical properties of these nanostructured materials are highly dependent on their dimensions, surface area, surface chemistry and the nature of the polymer backbone.
these nanofibrous and nanotubular structures are promising materials for future nanodevices and nanosystems.
the nanostructure of conducting polymer can be tailored to meet a wide variety of applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the physical properties of these nanofiber and nanotube materials are strongly size dependent and that the physical and chemical properties of these nanostructured materials can be tailored for specific applications by controlling their dimensions and surface chemistry.
these nanostructures can be used as a building block to construct a variety of nanodevices with unique properties and novel functions, and thus can be used in many emerging technologies.
the electronic transport properties of individual polymer nanofibers/nanotubes are strongly dependent on the diameter and length of the nanowires.
